works.title: Discrete-Variable Extremum Problems
works.abstract: This paper reviews some recent successes in the use of linear programming methods for the solution of discrete-variable extremum problems. One example of the use of the multistage approach of dynamic programming for this purpose is also discussed.

works.title: On the Number of Nonscalar Multiplications Necessary to Evaluate Polynomials
works.abstract: We present algorithms which use only $O(\sqrt n )$ nonscalar multiplications (i.e. multiplications involving “x” on both sides) to evaluate polynomials of degree n, and proofs that at least $\sqrt n $ are required. These results have practical application in the evaluation of matrix polynomials with scalar coefficients, since the “matrix $ \times $ matrix” multiplications are relatively expensive, and also in determining how many multiplications are needed for polynomials with rational coefficients, since multiplications by integers can in principle be replaced by several additions.

works.title: Trivial geometric heuristic for subset sum problem
works.abstract: All exact algorithms for solving subset sum problem (SUBSET\_SUM) are exponential (brute force, branch and bound search, dynamic programming which is pseudo-polynomial). To find the approximate solutions both a classical greedy algorithm and its improved variety, and different approximation schemes are used.This paper is an attempt to build another greedy algorithm by transferring representation of analytic geometry to such an object of discrete structure as a set. Set of size $n$ is identified with $n$-dimensional space with Euclidean metric, the subset-sum is identified with (hyper)plane.

works.title: EPR-C3: A Deterministic Constraint-Aware Heuristic for High-Dimensional Subset Selection in Multiple Linear Regression
works.abstract:
Abstract 
         Subset selection in multiple linear regression (MLR) is a statistical-computing challenge in high-dimensional data because candidate predictors expand the combinatorial search space and increase risks of multicollinearity, overfitting, and statistically inadmissible models. This study introduces EPR-C3, a deterministic multi-start neighborhood-search heuristic for constraint-aware subset selection in ordinary least squares (OLS)-based MLR. EPR-C3 combines structured exploration with reproducible local refinement through expansion, perturbation, reduction, and C3 constraint refinement, comprising correlation cleanup, replacement recovery, and variance inflation factor pruning, while preserving the native OLS formulation and explicit candidate equations. Benchmark analyses show that EPR-C3 recovers a high proportion of Top-K admissible subsets identified by exhaustive all-subsets regression while reducing computational cost in highly combinatorial problems. An empirical utility threshold is proposed to identify when heuristic search becomes preferable to exhaustive enumeration. Comparisons with stepwise procedures, penalized-regression preselection, filter-wrapper screening, genetic algorithms, and branch-and-bound subset selection show that embedding admissibility constraints within the search workflow improves the recovery--efficiency tradeoff. An applied case study demonstrates reproducible recovery of a published MLR equation with reduced runtime, supporting EPR-C3 as a deterministic statistical-computing heuristic for tractable subset selection in regression modeling and prediction.

works.title: Solving Subset Sum Problems using Binary Optimization with Applications in Auditing and Financial Data Analysis
works.abstract:
Many applications in automated auditing and the analysis and consistency
check of financial documents can be formulated in part as the subset sum
problem: Given a set of numbers and a target sum, find the subset of
numbers that sums up to the target. The problem is NP-hard and classical
solving algorithms are therefore not practical to use in real
applications. We tackle the problem as a QUBO (quadratic unconstrained
binary optimization) problem and show how gradient descent on Hopfield
Networks reliably finds solutions for both artificial and real data. We
give an outlook for the application of specialized hardware and quantum
algorithms.
